In mathematical [[set theory]], '''Zermelo's categoricity theorem''' was proved by [[Ernst Zermelo]] in 1930. It states that all models of a certain [[second-order logic|second-order]] version of the [[ZFC|Zermelo–Fraenkel axioms of set theory]] are isomorphic to a member of a certain [[class (set theory)|class]] of sets.

==Statement==

Let <math>\mathrm{ZFC}^2</math> denote Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory, but with a second-order version of the axiom of replacement formulated as follows:<ref>[[Stewart Shapiro|S. Shapiro]], ''Foundations Without Foundationalism: A Case for Second-order Logic'' (1991).</ref>

: <math>\forall F\forall x\exists y\forall z(z\in y \iff \exists w(w\in x\land z = F(w)))</math>

, namely the second-order universal closure of the [[axiom schema]] of replacement.<ref name="Uzquiano99">G. Uzquiano, "Models of Second-Order Zermelo Set Theory". [[Bulletin of Symbolic Logic]], vol. 5, no. 3 (1999), pp.289--302.</ref><sup>p.&nbsp;289</sup> Then every model of <math>\mathrm{ZFC}^2</math> is isomorphic to a set <math>V_\kappa</math> in the [[von Neumann hierarchy]], for some [[strongly inaccessible cardinal]] <math>\kappa</math>.<ref name="HamkinsSolberg22">{{cite arXiv|eprint=2009.07164 |author1=[[Joel David Hamkins]] |author2=Hans Robin Solberg |title=Categorical large cardinals and the tension between categoricity and set-theoretic reflection |date=2020 |class=math.LO }}, Theorem 1.</ref>

==Original presentation==

Zermelo originally considered a version of <math>\mathrm{ZFC}^2</math> with [[urelement]]s. Rather than using the modern satisfaction relation <math>\vDash</math>, he defines a "normal domain" to be a collection of sets along with the true <math>\in</math> relation that satisfies <math>\mathrm{ZFC}^2</math>.<ref name="MaddyVaananen23">{{cite arXiv|eprint=2204.13754 |last1=Maddy |first1=Penelope |author1link = Penelope Maddy|author2link = Jouko Väänänen|last2=Väänänen |first2=Jouko |title=Philosophical Uses of Categoricity Arguments |date=2022 |class=math.LO }}</ref><sup>p.&nbsp;9</sup>

==Related results==

[[Dedekind]] proved that the second-order [[Peano axioms]] hold in a model if and only if the model is isomorphic to the true natural numbers.<ref name="MaddyVaananen23" /><sup>pp.&nbsp;5–6</sup><ref name="HamkinsSolberg22" /><sup>p.&nbsp;1</sup> Uzquiano proved that when removing replacement from <math>\mathsf{ZFC}^2</math> and considering a second-order version of [[Zermelo set theory]] with a second-order version of [[Axiom schema of specification|separation]], there exist models not isomorphic to any <math>V_\delta</math> for a [[limit ordinal]] <math>\delta>\omega</math>.<ref>[[Akihiro Kanamori|A. Kanamori]], "Introductory note to 1930a". In ''[https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-540-79384-7 Ernst Zermelo - Collected Works/Gesammelte Werke]'' (2009), DOI 10.1007/978-3-540-79384-7.</ref><sup>p.&nbsp;396</sup>
